questions.question: Which statement best describes teacher autonomy in a professional context?

options.A: Freedom to act without any professional standards or institutional obligations
options.B: Professional discretion to make informed educational decisions within legitimate curricular, ethical and institutional frameworks
options.C: Authority to reject all forms of supervision
options.D: Freedom to teach only the content preferred by the teacher

questions.explanation: Teacher autonomy is professional discretion exercised within curricular, ethical, legal and institutional responsibilities. It is not unrestricted personal freedom.

questions.question: Which of the following is the clearest example of pedagogical autonomy?

options.A: A teacher selects an appropriate teaching strategy after assessing the learning needs of the class
options.B: A teacher ignores prescribed learning objectives
options.C: A teacher refuses to assess students
options.D: A teacher changes official school rules independently

questions.explanation: Pedagogical autonomy allows teachers to exercise professional judgement regarding teaching methods and classroom strategies while working towards prescribed educational objectives.

questions.question: Teacher autonomy is most defensible when professional decisions are primarily based on:

options.A: Personal convenience
options.B: Evidence, learner needs, professional knowledge and ethical considerations
options.C: Avoidance of accountability
options.D: Individual preference regardless of educational outcomes

questions.explanation: Professional autonomy derives legitimacy from specialised knowledge, evidence, ethical judgement and commitment to learners rather than personal convenience.

questions.question: Assertion A: Teacher autonomy and teacher accountability are not necessarily contradictory. Reason R: Professional autonomy permits informed discretion, while accountability requires teachers to justify decisions and accept responsibility for professional practice. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Professional autonomy and accountability are complementary when teachers have discretion but remain answerable for the quality, ethics and consequences of their professional decisions.

questions.question: Which situation represents responsible exercise of teacher autonomy?

options.A: Changing a teaching strategy because assessment evidence shows that students have not understood the concept
options.B: Omitting difficult portions of the curriculum permanently without educational justification
options.C: Refusing to maintain student records
options.D: Ignoring the learning needs of low-performing students

questions.explanation: Responsible autonomy involves adapting professional practice on the basis of evidence and learner needs while continuing to pursue legitimate curricular goals.

questions.question: Teacher accountability primarily means that a teacher is:

options.A: Answerable for professional decisions, duties and educational performance to legitimate stakeholders
options.B: Required to obey every instruction without professional judgement
options.C: Responsible only for examination marks
options.D: Free from review once appointed

questions.explanation: Accountability involves answerability for professional conduct, decisions, duties and performance to learners, institutions, authorities, parents and society within appropriate frameworks.

questions.question: Which distinction between accountability and responsibility is most appropriate?

options.A: Responsibility concerns duties and obligations, while accountability includes being answerable for how those duties are performed
options.B: Responsibility and accountability are completely unrelated
options.C: Accountability applies only to students
options.D: Responsibility means freedom from consequences

questions.explanation: Responsibility refers to professional duties and obligations. Accountability adds answerability for the manner in which those responsibilities are fulfilled and for relevant outcomes.

questions.question: A teacher completes the syllabus on schedule, but classroom evidence shows that a large number of students have not acquired expected competencies. Which response best reflects professional accountability?

options.A: Claim that syllabus completion alone ends the teacher's responsibility
options.B: Analyse learning evidence, identify difficulties and modify instruction or provide appropriate support
options.C: Blame students without investigation
options.D: Stop assessing the class

questions.explanation: Professional accountability focuses not merely on procedural completion but also on examining evidence of learning and taking reasonable corrective action.

questions.question: Which form of accountability is most directly involved when a teacher reflects critically on personal teaching effectiveness even without external inspection?

options.A: Professional or internal accountability
options.B: Market accountability
options.C: Financial accountability only
options.D: Political accountability only

questions.explanation: Professional accountability includes self-regulation, reflection and commitment to professional standards rather than dependence solely on external monitoring.

questions.question: Consider the following dimensions of teacher accountability: 1. Accountability to learners 2. Accountability to professional standards 3. Accountability to the institution and legitimate authorities 4. Accountability to society. Which are relevant?

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 1, 2 and 3 only
options.C: 2, 3 and 4 only

questions.explanation: Teacher accountability is multidimensional. Teachers have obligations towards learners, the profession, their institutions and the wider society served by education.

questions.question: Which approach to teacher accountability is most likely to promote genuine professional improvement?

options.A: Combining clear expectations, evidence, constructive feedback, professional support and appropriate consequences
options.B: Using punishment as the only mechanism
options.C: Ignoring performance entirely
options.D: Judging teachers solely by one examination score

questions.explanation: Developmental accountability combines expectations and evidence with feedback, support and proportionate consequences, encouraging improvement rather than mere compliance.

questions.question: Assertion A: Excessive external control can weaken meaningful teacher autonomy. Reason R: When every professional decision is prescribed in detail, teachers have little scope to exercise context-sensitive professional judgement. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Over-prescription can reduce teachers to procedural compliance and limit the professional discretion needed to respond to learner and classroom contexts.

questions.question: A school head requires every teacher to use exactly the same instructional method for every lesson regardless of subject, class or learner needs. Which professional concern is most evident?

options.A: Undue restriction of pedagogical autonomy
options.B: Excessive learner autonomy
options.C: Excessive financial decentralisation
options.D: Absence of curriculum

questions.explanation: Uniform prescription of teaching methods regardless of context restricts teachers' ability to exercise pedagogical judgement.

questions.question: Which condition most strongly supports responsible teacher autonomy?

options.A: Strong professional competence combined with clear ethical and institutional expectations
options.B: Absence of professional preparation
options.C: Complete absence of standards
options.D: No evaluation of teaching

questions.explanation: Autonomy is most productive when teachers possess strong professional knowledge and operate within clear standards, ethical principles and legitimate institutional expectations.

questions.question: Which teacher action most clearly demonstrates professional responsibility towards learners?

options.A: Providing fair learning opportunities and appropriate support while respecting learner dignity
options.B: Giving attention only to high achievers
options.C: Publicly humiliating students who perform poorly
options.D: Ignoring persistent learning difficulties

questions.explanation: Professional responsibility includes promoting learning, fairness, inclusion, support and respect for the dignity of every learner.

questions.question: A teacher discovers that an assessment item unfairly disadvantages a particular group of learners. What is the most professionally responsible response?

options.A: Review and revise the assessment while preserving legitimate learning objectives
options.B: Continue using it because it was already prepared
options.C: Ignore evidence of unfairness
options.D: Remove assessment entirely

questions.explanation: Professional responsibility requires teachers to examine fairness and validity and to correct assessment practices that unjustifiably disadvantage learners.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects collective professional responsibility in a school?

options.A: Teachers collaborate to improve learning and accept shared responsibility for broader school improvement
options.B: Every teacher is concerned only with personal classroom records
options.C: Teachers avoid discussing instructional problems with colleagues
options.D: School improvement is solely the head teacher's responsibility

questions.explanation: Professional responsibility can be collective as well as individual. Collaboration among teachers contributes to school-wide learning and improvement.

questions.question: Which of the following best represents ethical accountability?

options.A: Ensuring fairness, confidentiality, dignity and non-discrimination in professional conduct
options.B: Producing high examination scores by any means
options.C: Following orders even when they clearly violate learner dignity
options.D: Sharing confidential student information publicly

questions.explanation: Ethical accountability requires professional conduct consistent with principles such as fairness, dignity, confidentiality and non-discrimination.

questions.question: Assertion A: Teacher accountability should not be reduced to student examination results alone. Reason R: Student outcomes are influenced by multiple factors, and teacher professionalism includes responsibilities beyond test-score production. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Student achievement matters, but teacher accountability should use multiple indicators because learning is influenced by several factors and teaching includes broader professional obligations.

questions.question: Which combination provides the most balanced evidence for evaluating teacher accountability? 1. Classroom observation 2. Student learning evidence 3. Professional conduct and responsibilities 4. Teacher reflection and professional development.

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 1, 2 and 3 only
options.C: 2, 3 and 4 only

questions.explanation: A balanced accountability framework uses multiple sources rather than relying on a single measure. Teaching quality, learning evidence, professional conduct and professional growth are all relevant.

questions.question: A teacher consistently records low achievement among several students but makes no attempt to diagnose their difficulties or alter instruction. Which professional dimension is most directly weakened?

options.A: Responsibility for learner progress
options.B: Teacher autonomy itself
options.C: Financial autonomy
options.D: Institutional ownership

questions.explanation: Teachers are not responsible for guaranteeing identical outcomes, but they are professionally responsible for responding reasonably to evidence of learning difficulties.

questions.question: Which relationship among autonomy, competence and accountability is most appropriate?

options.A: Greater professional autonomy should be supported by competence and accompanied by accountability
options.B: Autonomy makes competence unnecessary
options.C: Accountability eliminates the need for professional judgement
options.D: Competence is unrelated to autonomy

questions.explanation: Professional autonomy is meaningful when practitioners possess the competence to exercise informed judgement and remain accountable for that judgement.

questions.question: A school introduces a new instructional programme. Teachers are encouraged to adapt classroom implementation according to learner needs but must document the adaptations and their outcomes. This arrangement best illustrates:

options.A: Autonomy with accountability
options.B: Autonomy without responsibility
options.C: Complete bureaucratic control
options.D: Absence of professional standards

questions.explanation: Teachers are given discretion to adapt practice while remaining answerable through documentation and evidence of outcomes. This combines autonomy with accountability.

questions.question: A Dy.E.O. wants to strengthen teacher accountability without creating a culture of fear. Which strategy is most appropriate?

options.A: Use transparent expectations, multiple sources of evidence, constructive feedback, professional support and fair review
options.B: Use surprise punishment as the principal strategy
options.C: Publish individual teacher rankings based solely on one student test
options.D: Remove all professional discretion from teachers

questions.explanation: Constructive accountability combines clear standards and evidence with support, feedback and fair procedures. Fear-based systems may encourage compliance or concealment rather than genuine improvement.

questions.question: A Dy.E.O. observes that teachers in a school follow every administrative instruction mechanically but rarely modify teaching when students fail to understand. Which reform would best strengthen teacher professionalism?

options.A: Develop teachers' capacity for evidence-based professional judgement while maintaining clear accountability for learner support
options.B: Issue increasingly detailed instructions for every classroom action
options.C: Remove teachers from all instructional decision-making
options.D: Evaluate teachers only through attendance records

questions.explanation: Teacher professionalism requires more than compliance. Teachers need competence and appropriate autonomy to make context-sensitive instructional decisions, together with accountability for responsible practice.

questions.question: Which situation best demonstrates professional rather than merely administrative accountability?

options.A: A teacher critically examines evidence of student learning and improves instruction even when no inspection is scheduled
options.B: A teacher prepares records only on the day of inspection
options.C: A teacher follows an order without considering its educational consequences
options.D: A teacher considers attendance alone as evidence of effective teaching

questions.explanation: Professional accountability includes internal commitment to standards, learner progress and continuous improvement, rather than compliance only when externally monitored.

questions.question: Which principle should guide a teacher when professional autonomy appears to conflict with an institutional instruction?

options.A: Examine the legitimate purpose, applicable rules, learner welfare and professional ethics before deciding how to act
options.B: Always ignore institutional instructions
options.C: Always obey without exercising professional judgement
options.D: Choose whichever action is personally easiest

questions.explanation: Professional autonomy operates within legitimate institutional, ethical and legal frameworks. Responsible judgement considers both professional obligations and learner welfare.

questions.question: Assertion A: Professional autonomy requires professional competence. Reason R: Meaningful professional discretion depends on the knowledge and judgement needed to choose among educational alternatives. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Autonomy without sufficient professional knowledge can become arbitrary decision-making. Competence provides the basis for informed professional judgement.

questions.question: Which action most clearly represents curricular autonomy within legitimate limits?

options.A: Selecting locally relevant examples and learning experiences to achieve prescribed curricular objectives
options.B: Discarding prescribed curricular objectives without justification
options.C: Refusing to teach a subject assigned to the teacher
options.D: Replacing the entire curriculum with personally preferred content

questions.explanation: Teachers may exercise professional discretion in contextualising curriculum and selecting learning experiences while remaining responsible for prescribed curricular purposes.

questions.question: A teacher uses locally familiar examples to explain an abstract concept while maintaining the intended learning outcome. This is best interpreted as:

options.A: Context-sensitive exercise of pedagogical autonomy
options.B: Violation of professional responsibility
options.C: Rejection of curriculum
options.D: Absence of accountability

questions.explanation: Professional autonomy enables teachers to adapt pedagogy to learners and context without abandoning legitimate curricular outcomes.

questions.question: Which form of accountability is most directly involved when teachers are expected to comply with legitimate service rules, institutional procedures and official duties?

options.A: Administrative accountability
options.B: Pedagogical autonomy
options.C: Market accountability
options.D: Learner autonomy

questions.explanation: Administrative accountability concerns answerability for compliance with legitimate institutional procedures, service obligations and administrative responsibilities.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes professional accountability from bureaucratic compliance?

options.A: Professional accountability involves informed commitment to educational standards and learner welfare, whereas bureaucratic compliance may focus primarily on following prescribed procedures
options.B: Professional accountability means ignoring all procedures
options.C: Bureaucratic compliance necessarily guarantees effective teaching
options.D: There is no conceptual difference between the two

questions.explanation: Compliance with legitimate procedures is important, but professional accountability extends further to judgement, ethics, learner welfare and quality of practice.

questions.question: A teacher maintains every required register accurately but repeatedly uses ineffective teaching practices and ignores evidence of poor learning. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

options.A: Administrative compliance is present, but broader professional accountability is weak
options.B: Complete professional accountability has been achieved
options.C: Student learning is irrelevant to teacher responsibility
options.D: Accurate records eliminate the need for effective instruction

questions.explanation: Teacher accountability includes administrative duties but cannot be reduced to record maintenance. Quality of teaching and appropriate responses to learner needs are also important.

questions.question: Consider the following features of responsible teacher autonomy: 1. Professional competence 2. Evidence-based judgement 3. Ethical conduct 4. Answerability for decisions. Which are essential?

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 1, 2 and 3 only
options.C: 2, 3 and 4 only

questions.explanation: Responsible autonomy combines competence, evidence, ethics and accountability. Removing any of these weakens the professional basis of autonomous decision-making.

questions.question: Which teacher behaviour best represents accountability to parents without compromising professional autonomy?

options.A: Communicating learner progress transparently while using professional judgement about appropriate instructional decisions
options.B: Allowing every parent to determine classroom grades
options.C: Refusing to communicate with parents
options.D: Changing assessment results whenever a parent demands it

questions.explanation: Teachers should communicate appropriately with parents and remain answerable for learner progress while retaining legitimate professional judgement over teaching and assessment.

questions.question: A teacher notices that personal expectations are influencing the amount of attention given to different groups of students. Which response best demonstrates professional responsibility?

options.A: Reflect on the bias and deliberately adopt fairer participation and support practices
options.B: Continue the practice because teachers have complete autonomy
options.C: Stop interacting with students
options.D: Assume professional bias cannot affect learning

questions.explanation: Professional responsibility includes reflective examination of one's own practices and correction of biases that may undermine fairness or learner opportunity.

questions.question: Assertion A: Teacher responsibility extends beyond transmitting subject content. Reason R: Teachers also have professional obligations relating to learner welfare, inclusion, assessment, ethical conduct and educational development. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Teaching is a multidimensional professional role involving instruction as well as assessment, inclusion, learner support, ethical conduct and wider educational responsibilities.

questions.question: Which practice most strongly supports teacher self-accountability?

options.A: Systematic reflection using evidence from teaching and student learning
options.B: Waiting for inspection before examining teaching quality
options.C: Avoiding feedback from colleagues
options.D: Maintaining the same method regardless of results

questions.explanation: Self-accountability involves internally driven reflection, evidence use and improvement rather than dependence entirely on external supervision.

questions.question: Which school culture is most likely to strengthen both teacher autonomy and accountability?

options.A: A culture of professional trust, collaboration, evidence use, clear expectations and constructive review
options.B: A culture in which teachers never discuss their practice
options.C: A culture based entirely on fear of punishment
options.D: A culture with neither expectations nor review

questions.explanation: Professional trust combined with clear expectations, collaboration and evidence-based review allows teachers to exercise judgement while remaining responsible for practice.

questions.question: Which statement best explains the role of professional trust in teacher autonomy?

options.A: Trust permits appropriate professional discretion but does not remove the need for evidence or accountability
options.B: Trust means teachers should never be evaluated
options.C: Trust eliminates professional standards
options.D: Trust requires administrators to ignore misconduct

questions.explanation: Professional trust supports autonomy when teachers are treated as competent professionals, but trust operates alongside standards, evidence and accountability.

questions.question: A school head delegates instructional decisions to experienced teachers but regularly reviews learner evidence with them. Which leadership approach is most consistent with responsible autonomy?

options.A: Professional empowerment combined with accountability
options.B: Laissez-faire abandonment of responsibility
options.C: Complete centralisation
options.D: Punitive supervision

questions.explanation: Responsible empowerment provides teachers with meaningful professional discretion while retaining collaborative review of evidence and outcomes.

questions.question: Which accountability mechanism is most likely to distort teacher behaviour if used as the sole measure of performance?

options.A: A single high-stakes student test score
options.B: Multiple sources of evidence
options.C: Reflective self-evaluation
options.D: Constructive classroom observation

questions.explanation: Reliance on one high-stakes indicator may narrow teaching and overlook contextual factors and other dimensions of professional practice.

questions.question: A teacher is evaluated only on the percentage of students passing an examination. Which major limitation does this accountability model have?

options.A: It reduces complex professional performance to a single outcome indicator
options.B: It uses too many indicators
options.C: It gives excessive importance to professional ethics
options.D: It necessarily measures classroom processes accurately

questions.explanation: Teacher performance is multidimensional. A single examination indicator cannot adequately represent pedagogy, inclusion, professional conduct, learner growth and contextual factors.

questions.question: Which combination would provide the most defensible basis for reviewing teacher performance? 1. Classroom processes 2. Evidence of learner progress 3. Professional responsibilities 4. Contextual factors affecting teaching.

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 1, 2 and 3 only
options.C: 2, 3 and 4 only

questions.explanation: A fair review should use multiple dimensions and take relevant context into account rather than reducing professional performance to one measure.

questions.question: Which action most clearly violates professional responsibility regarding student information?

options.A: Publicly sharing confidential personal information without legitimate educational justification
options.B: Maintaining records securely
options.C: Sharing necessary information through authorised professional channels
options.D: Protecting learner privacy

questions.explanation: Teachers have a professional responsibility to protect confidentiality and disclose student information only through appropriate and legitimate channels.

questions.question: Assertion A: Transparency can strengthen teacher accountability. Reason R: Appropriate transparency enables legitimate stakeholders to understand professional expectations, processes and evidence while preserving necessary confidentiality. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Transparency supports answerability and trust, but it should operate alongside ethical obligations such as protection of confidential learner information.

questions.question: A teacher realises after reviewing assessment data that the teaching strategy used was ineffective. Which action best reflects reflective professional responsibility?

options.A: Acknowledge the evidence, identify possible causes and redesign instruction
options.B: Alter the marks to make the results appear better
options.C: Hide the assessment evidence
options.D: Continue the same method solely to avoid admitting difficulty

questions.explanation: Reflective professionalism requires honest use of evidence and willingness to improve practice when existing approaches are ineffective.

questions.question: A Dy.E.O. observes that teachers are reluctant to experiment with better teaching methods because every unsuccessful attempt is treated as misconduct. What is the most likely consequence?

options.A: A punitive accountability culture may suppress responsible professional innovation
options.B: Teacher autonomy will necessarily increase
options.C: Professional trust will automatically strengthen
options.D: Innovation will become completely risk-free

questions.explanation: When reasonable professional experimentation is punished merely because it does not immediately succeed, teachers may avoid innovation and focus on defensive compliance.

questions.question: What should a Dy.E.O. do when classroom observations reveal a genuine professional weakness rather than deliberate negligence?

options.A: Combine clear performance expectations with mentoring, professional development and subsequent review
options.B: Immediately treat every weakness as misconduct
options.C: Ignore the weakness permanently
options.D: Remove all autonomy from every teacher in the school

questions.explanation: Developmental accountability distinguishes professional capacity gaps from misconduct and uses support, clear expectations and follow-up to improve performance.

questions.question: A Dy.E.O. is designing a teacher accountability system. Which model would best balance autonomy, responsibility and improvement?

options.A: Clear professional standards, appropriate teacher discretion, multiple evidence sources, constructive feedback, support and fair consequences
options.B: Complete teacher freedom with no review
options.C: Detailed control of every classroom decision with no teacher discretion
options.D: Teacher ranking based solely on raw examination pass percentages

questions.explanation: A balanced professional accountability system combines legitimate autonomy with clear responsibilities, multiple forms of evidence, developmental support and fair answerability.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes professional responsibility from mere task completion?

options.A: Professional responsibility requires attention to the quality, ethics and educational consequences of one's work, not merely completion of assigned tasks
options.B: Professional responsibility ends whenever an assigned task is recorded as completed
options.C: Professional responsibility concerns only attendance
options.D: Task completion always guarantees effective teaching

questions.explanation: Professional responsibility extends beyond procedural compliance to the quality, ethics and educational consequences of professional practice.

questions.question: A teacher regularly completes lesson plans but rarely modifies them even when classroom evidence shows that learners are confused. Which professional principle is most clearly neglected?

options.A: Responsive professional responsibility
options.B: Financial accountability
options.C: Institutional ownership
options.D: Administrative decentralisation

questions.explanation: Responsible teaching requires responsiveness to evidence of learner understanding rather than mechanical adherence to predetermined plans.

questions.question: Which of the following most appropriately limits teacher autonomy?

options.A: Learner rights, professional ethics, legitimate curriculum requirements and applicable institutional rules
options.B: Personal preferences of every observer
options.C: The requirement that all teachers use identical methods in every situation
options.D: The assumption that teachers possess no professional judgement

questions.explanation: Teacher autonomy is bounded by legitimate professional, ethical, curricular and institutional obligations, particularly the rights and welfare of learners.

questions.question: Assertion A: Teacher autonomy cannot legitimately be used to justify discriminatory classroom practices. Reason R: Professional autonomy is constrained by ethical obligations concerning fairness, dignity and learner rights. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Professional autonomy does not override ethical duties. Discrimination violates fairness, dignity and the rights of learners.

questions.question: A teacher gives additional instructional support to learners who have fallen behind. Some argue that every learner should receive exactly the same amount of support. Which principle best justifies the teacher's decision?

options.A: Equitable professional responsibility may require differentiated support according to learner need
options.B: Teacher autonomy permits arbitrary favouritism
options.C: Accountability requires identical treatment in all circumstances
options.D: Professional responsibility applies only to high achievers

questions.explanation: Fairness does not always require identical treatment. Responsible teachers may provide differentiated support where learners have different educational needs.

questions.question: Which teacher action best represents accountability for assessment?

options.A: Using fair assessment procedures, maintaining accurate evidence and providing appropriate feedback
options.B: Changing marks to satisfy external pressure
options.C: Using assessment only to punish learners
options.D: Refusing to explain assessment criteria

questions.explanation: Assessment accountability includes fairness, validity, accurate records, transparency of appropriate criteria and useful feedback.

questions.question: A teacher deliberately awards higher marks to certain students because of personal relationships. Which dimensions of professionalism are most directly violated?

options.A: Ethical responsibility and assessment accountability
options.B: Pedagogical autonomy only
options.C: Curricular flexibility only
options.D: Professional development only

questions.explanation: Biased grading violates fairness, professional ethics and the teacher's accountability for valid and impartial assessment.

questions.question: Which statement best represents accountability for continuous professional development?

options.A: Teachers should continually update professional knowledge and skills needed to fulfil their educational responsibilities
options.B: Initial qualification makes further learning unnecessary
options.C: Professional development is unrelated to teacher responsibility
options.D: Only inexperienced teachers require professional learning

questions.explanation: Professional responsibility includes maintaining and improving competence as knowledge, curricula, learner needs and educational practices change.

questions.question: Consider the following as elements of teacher professional responsibility: 1. Maintaining subject and pedagogical competence 2. Protecting learner dignity 3. Using assessment responsibly 4. Participating in appropriate professional development. Which are correct?

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 1, 2 and 3 only
options.C: 2, 3 and 4 only

questions.explanation: Teacher responsibility is multidimensional and includes competence, ethical treatment of learners, sound assessment and continuing professional growth.

questions.question: Which situation best demonstrates accountability to the teaching profession itself?

options.A: Maintaining professional standards and avoiding conduct that undermines the integrity of teaching
options.B: Seeking examination results by any means
options.C: Ignoring professional ethics whenever convenient
options.D: Sharing confidential information for personal benefit

questions.explanation: Teachers have responsibilities not only to particular institutions but also to uphold the standards, ethics and integrity of their profession.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate relationship between teacher autonomy and curriculum?

options.A: Teachers exercise professional judgement in interpreting and implementing curriculum while remaining accountable to legitimate curricular aims
options.B: Autonomy means teachers may disregard every curricular requirement
options.C: Curriculum eliminates all need for teacher judgement
options.D: Autonomy and curriculum cannot coexist

questions.explanation: Curriculum establishes educational purposes and expectations, while professional teachers exercise context-sensitive judgement in translating them into classroom learning.

questions.question: A prescribed textbook contains an example that is inappropriate for the local context. The teacher substitutes a more relevant example without changing the intended concept. This is best regarded as:

options.A: Legitimate contextualisation through professional autonomy
options.B: Automatic professional misconduct
options.C: Rejection of accountability
options.D: Abandonment of curriculum

questions.explanation: Contextual adaptation that preserves the intended learning goal is an appropriate exercise of pedagogical and curricular judgement.

questions.question: Assertion A: Standardisation and teacher autonomy need not always be mutually exclusive. Reason R: A system may establish common learning expectations while allowing teachers discretion in how those expectations are achieved. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Common standards can define expected outcomes while teachers retain appropriate autonomy over pedagogy, examples, pacing and learner support.

questions.question: Which accountability system is most likely to encourage 'teaching to the test'?

options.A: One that attaches very high consequences to a narrow set of test-score indicators
options.B: One that uses multiple evidence sources and classroom observations
options.C: One that encourages reflective professional practice
options.D: One that considers learner growth and context

questions.explanation: When accountability depends heavily on narrow high-stakes measures, teachers may concentrate disproportionately on tested content at the expense of broader educational aims.

questions.question: A teacher's students show limited progress. Before attributing the result entirely to teacher performance, an administrator should:

options.A: Examine teaching evidence together with learner starting points, attendance, resources and other relevant contextual factors
options.B: Assume the teacher alone determines every learning outcome
options.C: Ignore classroom practice completely
options.D: Use only the final examination average

questions.explanation: Teacher practice is important, but fair accountability recognises that learning outcomes are influenced by multiple factors. Multiple evidence sources are therefore needed.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes developmental accountability?

options.A: It uses accountability evidence not only for judgement but also to identify support and improve professional practice
options.B: It avoids all evaluation
options.C: It relies exclusively on punishment
options.D: It assumes every performance problem is deliberate misconduct

questions.explanation: Developmental accountability combines answerability with diagnosis, feedback, support and professional improvement.

questions.question: Which situation requires corrective accountability rather than professional development alone?

options.A: A teacher knowingly falsifies official assessment records
options.B: A newly appointed teacher needs support with classroom management
options.C: A teacher seeks help using a new teaching strategy
options.D: A teacher requests mentoring in assessment design

questions.explanation: Deliberate falsification is an ethical and professional breach and requires appropriate corrective accountability. Genuine capacity gaps are more appropriately addressed through support and development.

questions.question: Which distinction is most important when a school leader responds to weak teacher performance?

options.A: Distinguishing lack of professional capacity from deliberate negligence or misconduct
options.B: Treating every weakness as identical
options.C: Assuming support is never useful
options.D: Ignoring the cause of the problem

questions.explanation: Appropriate accountability requires diagnosis. Capacity gaps may require mentoring and development, whereas deliberate negligence or misconduct may require corrective action.

questions.question: Consider the following characteristics of a fair teacher accountability system: 1. Clear expectations 2. Multiple sources of evidence 3. Opportunity for professional support 4. Transparent and fair procedures. Which are desirable?

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 1, 2 and 3 only
options.C: 2, 3 and 4 only

questions.explanation: Fair accountability requires clarity, adequate evidence, developmental support and transparent procedures rather than arbitrary judgement.

questions.question: Assertion A: Accountability based entirely on external inspection may fail to produce sustained professional improvement. Reason R: Sustainable professionalism also requires internal commitment, reflection and self-regulation. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: External accountability has a role, but lasting professional quality also depends on internal professional standards, reflection and self-regulation.

questions.question: A school has excellent teacher attendance records but persistently weak classroom instruction. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

options.A: Attendance is one accountability indicator but cannot by itself establish professional effectiveness
options.B: Excellent attendance proves excellent teaching
options.C: Classroom instruction is unrelated to accountability
options.D: No further evidence is necessary

questions.explanation: Teacher attendance is necessary but professional accountability also concerns instructional quality, learner support, ethical conduct and other responsibilities.

questions.question: A head teacher wants teachers to take greater responsibility for school improvement. Which strategy is most likely to help?

options.A: Provide meaningful participation in professional decisions together with shared responsibility for agreed outcomes
options.B: Exclude teachers from all decision-making
options.C: Make the head teacher solely responsible for every outcome
options.D: Prevent collaboration among teachers

questions.explanation: Professional participation can strengthen ownership and collective responsibility when teachers also remain accountable for agreed educational goals.

questions.question: Which statement best explains collective teacher autonomy?

options.A: Teachers participate professionally as a group in appropriate curricular, instructional and school-improvement decisions
options.B: Every teacher acts independently without coordination
options.C: Teachers replace all legitimate administrative authority
options.D: Teachers are free from shared professional standards

questions.explanation: Autonomy may be exercised collectively through professional collaboration and participation in decisions affecting teaching, curriculum and school improvement.

questions.question: A Dy.E.O. finds that teachers are submitting identical lesson plans copied from a standard source, although their classrooms have very different learning needs. Which intervention is most appropriate?

options.A: Encourage context-sensitive planning based on learner evidence while maintaining accountability to curricular objectives
options.B: Require even more identical planning regardless of context
options.C: Stop lesson planning entirely
options.D: Judge planning only by the number of pages submitted

questions.explanation: Professional planning should respond to actual learners and contexts. Accountability should focus on educational purpose and quality rather than mechanical uniformity.

questions.question: A Dy.E.O. wants to determine whether greater teacher autonomy has actually improved professional practice. Which evidence would be most useful?

options.A: Changes in instructional quality, teacher decision-making, responsiveness to learner needs, professional collaboration and learning evidence
options.B: Only the number of circulars issued
options.C: Only teacher attendance
options.D: Only the number of lesson plans submitted

questions.explanation: The impact of autonomy should be examined through professional practice and its educational consequences rather than through administrative counts alone.

questions.question: Which statement best describes professional responsibility for inclusive teaching?

options.A: Teachers should identify and reduce avoidable barriers to participation and learning
options.B: Teachers are responsible only for students who learn easily
options.C: Inclusion is unrelated to classroom teaching
options.D: All learners should be taught identically regardless of need

questions.explanation: Professional responsibility includes creating fair opportunities to participate and learn by responding appropriately to learner diversity and barriers.

questions.question: A teacher discovers that a learner with a disability cannot access a classroom activity. Which response most clearly reflects professional responsibility?

options.A: Adapt the activity or provide appropriate support while preserving the intended learning goal
options.B: Exclude the learner from the activity
options.C: Lower every learning expectation for the entire class
options.D: Ignore the barrier because the same activity was given to everyone

questions.explanation: Responsible inclusive practice removes unnecessary barriers while maintaining legitimate educational goals.

questions.question: Assertion A: Teacher autonomy can contribute to inclusion. Reason R: Teachers may use professional judgement to adapt pedagogy and support according to diverse learner needs. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Appropriate autonomy enables teachers to make context-sensitive instructional adaptations that support diverse learners.

questions.question: Which situation most clearly represents misuse of teacher autonomy?

options.A: A teacher refuses to provide required learning opportunities because of personal prejudice
options.B: A teacher changes examples to suit learner context
options.C: A teacher differentiates instruction based on assessment evidence
options.D: A teacher selects an appropriate classroom activity

questions.explanation: Professional autonomy cannot justify prejudicial or discriminatory decisions that violate learner rights and professional ethics.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate basis for holding a teacher accountable for a professional decision?

options.A: Whether the decision was informed, ethical, reasonable and consistent with professional obligations
options.B: Whether every observer personally agrees with it
options.C: Whether it was the easiest option
options.D: Whether it avoided all professional risk

questions.explanation: Accountability should examine the quality and legitimacy of professional judgement, not demand identical decisions in every complex situation.

questions.question: Which statement best describes accountability to learners?

options.A: Teachers are answerable for providing fair, respectful and professionally competent educational opportunities
options.B: Teachers must guarantee identical achievement by every learner
options.C: Teachers must accept every learner demand
options.D: Teacher accountability ends once attendance is recorded

questions.explanation: Teachers are responsible for professional opportunities and practices, but they cannot guarantee identical outcomes because learning depends on multiple factors.

questions.question: A teacher reports that a class has weak foundational skills and requests additional instructional time and support. Which professional quality is most evident?

options.A: Responsible use of evidence and professional voice
options.B: Avoidance of accountability
options.C: Administrative insubordination
options.D: Lack of teacher autonomy

questions.explanation: Professional responsibility includes identifying learner needs, using evidence and communicating legitimate instructional requirements.

questions.question: Consider the following responsibilities of teachers towards the school as an organisation: 1. Collaboration with colleagues 2. Participation in legitimate institutional responsibilities 3. Accurate professional records 4. Contribution to school improvement. Which are relevant?

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 1, 2 and 3 only
options.C: 2, 3 and 4 only

questions.explanation: Teacher responsibility includes classroom work as well as appropriate institutional collaboration, documentation and participation in school improvement.

questions.question: Which school practice most strongly encourages collective accountability?

options.A: Teachers jointly analyse learning evidence and plan improvement strategies
options.B: Teachers work in complete professional isolation
options.C: Every teacher hides classroom problems from colleagues
options.D: Only the head teacher reviews student learning

questions.explanation: Collective accountability develops when teachers share evidence, responsibility and professional action for improving learning.

questions.question: Assertion A: Collaboration can strengthen rather than weaken teacher autonomy. Reason R: Professional autonomy can include collective professional judgement, not merely isolated individual decision-making. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Professional autonomy can operate individually and collectively. Collaborative judgement can strengthen the quality and legitimacy of professional decisions.

questions.question: Which accountability practice is most likely to encourage defensive behaviour rather than genuine improvement?

options.A: Public humiliation based on a narrow performance measure
options.B: Confidential professional feedback supported by evidence
options.C: Mentoring followed by review
options.D: Collaborative examination of learning evidence

questions.explanation: Punitive and humiliating accountability can encourage concealment, fear and defensive compliance rather than honest reflection and improvement.

questions.question: A teacher receives constructive feedback after classroom observation and then experiments with an improved strategy. Which accountability function is illustrated?

options.A: Developmental accountability
options.B: Punitive accountability only
options.C: Financial accountability
options.D: Absence of accountability

questions.explanation: Developmental accountability uses evidence and feedback to improve professional practice rather than focusing solely on judgement or punishment.

questions.question: Which relationship between supervision and autonomy is most appropriate?

options.A: Supportive supervision can strengthen professional autonomy by improving competence and judgement
options.B: Any supervision automatically destroys autonomy
options.C: Autonomy requires complete absence of professional review
options.D: Supervision should control every instructional decision

questions.explanation: Supervision need not be controlling. Supportive supervision can develop professional competence, reflection and responsible autonomy.

questions.question: A head teacher gives teachers freedom to choose instructional strategies but provides no curriculum guidance, professional support or review. Which description is most accurate?

options.A: Freedom without sufficient professional support or accountability
options.B: Ideal responsible autonomy
options.C: Strong developmental supervision
options.D: High administrative accountability

questions.explanation: Responsible autonomy requires not only discretion but also competence, expectations, support and accountability.

questions.question: Which principle should guide accountability when student outcomes are affected by factors beyond the teacher's control?

options.A: Use multiple sources of evidence and assess the quality of professional action within the relevant context
options.B: Hold the teacher solely responsible for every outcome
options.C: Ignore student learning completely
options.D: Use one raw score regardless of context

questions.explanation: Fair accountability recognises contextual influences while still examining whether teachers have acted competently and responsibly within their professional role.

questions.question: Which is the best example of accountability for professional growth?

options.A: A teacher identifies a weakness, undertakes relevant training and demonstrates improvement in practice
options.B: A teacher refuses all feedback after appointment
options.C: A teacher attends training only to obtain a certificate without applying learning
options.D: A teacher assumes experience makes further learning unnecessary

questions.explanation: Professional growth accountability concerns identifying needs, engaging meaningfully in development and improving practice.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the idea of teacher agency?

options.A: The capacity of teachers to act intentionally and professionally to influence educational practice within contextual constraints
options.B: Freedom from every institutional requirement
options.C: Complete control over educational policy
options.D: Mechanical implementation of instructions without judgement

questions.explanation: Teacher agency refers to the capacity to exercise purposeful professional action within social, institutional and policy contexts.

questions.question: Which school condition is most likely to strengthen teacher agency?

options.A: Professional trust, access to evidence, collaboration and meaningful participation in decisions
options.B: Rigid prohibition of teacher input
options.C: Punishment for all professional experimentation
options.D: Complete isolation among teachers

questions.explanation: Teacher agency grows where teachers have competence, information, professional voice, collaboration and legitimate scope for action.

questions.question: Assertion A: Teacher agency and accountability can reinforce each other. Reason R: Teachers who have meaningful professional voice can take greater ownership of decisions and outcomes when expectations are clear. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

questions.explanation: Meaningful professional participation can strengthen ownership and responsibility, provided autonomy operates within clear standards and accountability.

questions.question: A Dy.E.O. observes that teachers rarely discuss learning problems because they fear that admitting difficulties will be used against them. Which issue is most evident?

options.A: Low psychological safety is weakening professional accountability and collaborative improvement
options.B: Teachers have excessive curricular autonomy
options.C: The school has too much professional trust
options.D: Accountability is unnecessary

questions.explanation: When professionals fear punishment for honest discussion of problems, evidence may be hidden and opportunities for collective improvement are reduced.

questions.question: What should a Dy.E.O. do to encourage honest professional self-evaluation among teachers?

options.A: Create clear standards and supportive review processes in which evidence of weakness leads first to appropriate improvement support unless misconduct is involved
options.B: Punish every admission of difficulty
options.C: Eliminate all evaluation
options.D: Use only anonymous examination scores

questions.explanation: Constructive accountability encourages honest evidence use by distinguishing developmental needs from misconduct and providing appropriate support.

questions.question: A Dy.E.O. finds that a school has detailed accountability records but no evidence that the information is used to improve teaching. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

options.A: Accountability has become procedural rather than developmental
options.B: The accountability system is necessarily excellent
options.C: Teaching improvement is unrelated to accountability
options.D: More paperwork alone will solve the problem

questions.explanation: Accountability data have limited professional value if they are collected only for compliance and not used for reflection, support or improvement.

questions.question: Which sequence best represents a professional accountability cycle?

options.A: Set expectations, collect evidence, reflect and review, support improvement, follow up
options.B: Punish first, identify expectations later, avoid evidence
options.C: Collect records, store them permanently, take no action
options.D: Allow complete autonomy with no expectations or review

questions.explanation: Effective accountability is cyclical and uses clear expectations, evidence, reflection, improvement action and follow-up.

questions.question: A Dy.E.O. wants to distinguish a highly autonomous professional teacher from an unaccountable teacher. Which evidence is most decisive?

options.A: The teacher exercises informed discretion, can justify decisions with evidence and ethics, and responds to outcomes
options.B: The teacher makes every decision alone
options.C: The teacher never follows institutional expectations
options.D: The teacher avoids all documentation and review

questions.explanation: Professional autonomy is distinguished from unaccountability by competence, justification, ethical responsibility and answerability for professional decisions.

questions.question: A Dy.E.O. is evaluating whether a school has achieved a healthy balance among teacher autonomy, accountability and responsibility. Which evidence would be most comprehensive?

options.A: Teachers exercise professional judgement, follow ethical and curricular obligations, use evidence, collaborate, support diverse learners and remain answerable through fair review
options.B: Teachers follow every instruction mechanically
options.C: Teachers work without any supervision or professional standards
options.D: Teacher performance is judged only by attendance and examination pass percentage

questions.explanation: A healthy professional system combines discretion with competence, ethics, evidence, collaboration, learner responsibility and fair accountability.
